repos/trade-imports-address-book is a small Java / Spring Boot service: the org-scoped address book API and system of record for address records (MongoDB). Paths below are from the repo root. Production code is about 1,900 lines under src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/: address/ (10 files, about 1,065 lines: Address entity, AddressRequest create/update body with Bean Validation messages, AddressStatus, OperatorResponse, OperatorPageResponse, OperatorMapper, AddressExpiryIndex, OperatorRepository, OperatorService 222 lines, OperatorController 367 lines with five endpoints under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses: GET list (page, q, countryCode), POST create, GET /{operator-id}, PUT /{operator-id}, DELETE /{operator-id}), exceptions/ (5 files, about 245 lines: RFC 7807 problem and validation-problem responses), filter/ (3 files, about 260 lines; IdentityHeaderFilter enforces the caller organisation header), configuration/ (Mongo, address TTL, Jackson, OpenAPI, metrics, proxy, TLS), service/EmfMetricsPublisher. Config: src/main/resources/application.yml (120 lines) and compose/mongo/10-init.js. Contract: docs/openapi/operators.yml (491 lines) and docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (441 lines). Tests: 16 integration tests under src/test/java/.../integration/ and unit tests under src/test/java/.../address, exceptions, filter (about 3,800 lines on the address domain). README.md (274 lines) documents the API overview, security and trust boundary, soft delete (tombstones), non-prod address expiry and indexes. Rulings: there is no rulings ledger file in the repo; rulings appear inline in code comments and schema descriptions as cv-NNN references (for example cv-011 countryCode stored as given, cv-044 address book is untyped and unroled, cv-048 countryCode filter is resolved by the frontend), and each part claims the cv-NNN rulings in its own files. Scope leaves out: CI workflows (.github/), Dockerfile, docker/dev-run.sh, compose.yml and compose/floci, proxy, TLS, metrics, logging, tracing and health-check plumbing (configuration/ProxyConfig, tls/, MetricsConfig, OpenApiConfig, JacksonConfig, AwsConfig, filter/RequestTracingFilter, filter/HealthCheckFilter, service/EmfMetricsPublisher and their tests), and docs/review/ (EUDPA-58-review.md and items.trade-imports-address-book.json, a closed code-review ledger whose 190 items are all Fix/Done or Auto-Resolved, with no won't-fix judgement that departs from the code). Cut into 4 parts along the API's own seams: the address record and its validation, the single-address lifecycle (create, read, update, delete), listing and search, and organisation scoping and caller identity.

Extracted in 4 parts:
Part 1, The address record and its validation: Part 1, the address record and its validation. Read in full: address/Address.java (the persisted entity, 80 lines), address/AddressRequest.java (the create/update body with its Bean Validation constraints and messages, 108 lines), address/AddressStatus.java (ACTIVE, DELETED), address/OperatorResponse.java (the wire response with its null guards), address/OperatorMapper.java (entity to response and request to entity mapping), address/AddressExpiryIndex.java (the non-prod TTL index), configuration/AddressTtlConfig.java and configuration/MongoConfig.java, src/main/resources/application.yml (Mongo and address-book.ttl keys; CDP, AWS, logging, actuator and springdoc keys are out of this part's scope and only noted), compose/mongo/10-init.js (an empty template comment, no seed data), the README sections MongoDB, Soft delete (tombstones), Address expiry (non-prod only) and Indexes, and the AddressRequest and OperatorResponse schemas in docs/openapi/operators.yml. Tests read in full: AddressRequestValidationTest (the field-table validation matrix: 7 blank-field cases, 8 over-length cases, 1 malformed email, stray type and role, 8 at-max cases, countryCode presence-only and phone free-text), OperatorMapperTest (8 tests), OperatorResponseTest (11 guarded-null cases plus optional nulls), AddressExpiryIndexTest (6 tests), AddressTtlConfigTest (11 tests), AddressExpiryIT (3 tests) and OperatorIndexIT (1 test). Claims run in this order: the record's shape and rulings (cv-011, cv-016, cv-044), each request field's required flag, length limit and error message, the type and role rejection, server-assigned fields being ignored, the response shape and the deleted flag, update replace semantics, the status values, persistence (database, collection, the one compound index, auditing), then the non-prod expiry rule and its config keys, and what each test proves. The expireAt stamping on create is coded in OperatorService (part 2); it is claimed here from the README and AddressExpiryIT, which sit in this part's read.
Part 2, Single-address lifecycle: create, read, update, delete: Part 2 of 4 (single-address lifecycle). Read in full: address/OperatorController.java (367 lines: five handlers under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses, of which create, get, update and delete are this part's; list is part 3's and the authoriseOrg path-versus-header guard is part 4's), address/OperatorService.java (222 lines: create, get, update, delete, stampExpiry; list is part 3's), address/OperatorRepository.java (49 lines: org-scoped finders and save only), exceptions/Problem.java, ValidationProblem.java, GlobalExceptionHandler.java (173 lines, seven handlers), BadRequestException.java and NotFoundException.java, docs/openapi/operators.yml (491 lines, springdoc-generated) and docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (441 lines, hand-authored lock), the README 'API overview' section plus its 'Soft delete (tombstones)' and 'OpenAPI contract' sections, and seven test classes in full: AddressCrudIT (8 tests), AddressGetIT (3), AddressUpdateIT (8), AddressDeleteIT (7), OperatorComplianceIT (6), OperatorServiceTest (single-address cases: 5 create, 3 get, 5 update, 3 delete; its 11 list cases are part 3's) and GlobalExceptionHandlerTest (10). Covered: POST create (201, Location header, organisationId and ACTIVE stamping, ignored read-only fields, non-prod expiry stamp, every 400 shape, 404, 500), GET one (200 live, 200 tombstone with deleted true, 404 unknown or other organisation), PUT full replace (cleared optionals, server-owned fields preserved, modifiedAt bump, 400, 404 for unknown, other-organisation or tombstone, 409 optimistic-lock conflict, tombstone resurrection blocked), DELETE soft delete (204, status flip, modifiedAt bump, idempotent repeat with no re-save, list exclusion, get-after-delete, 404), the RFC 9457 problem and validation-problem shapes with every exception mapping, the cv-001, cv-010, cv-011, cv-016 and cv-040 rulings these four operations cite, and the contract lock tests. Two contract discrepancies are recorded as claims: the Location header is described as absolute in the generated spec and relative in the locked contract, and countryCode carries maxLength 2 only in the locked contract.
Part 3, Listing and searching addresses: Part 3, listing and searching addresses (repo at HEAD 83fd1dd). Read in full: address/OperatorController.java (367 lines; claimed only the list handler, lines 70-132), address/OperatorService.java (222 lines; claimed list, queryPage and toPartialMatchRegex, lines 37-117), address/OperatorRepository.java (49 lines; claimed the three search queries and the status finder), address/OperatorPageResponse.java (45 lines), docs/openapi/operators.yml (491 lines; the GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses operation and the OperatorPageResponse schema), docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml (441 lines; its description's Search and Pagination conventions and the list operation), README.md section API overview (lines 111-160; list row, list query parameters, wire conventions), and the tests OperatorListIT (9 tests), AddressSearchIT (10 tests), OperatorRepositoryIT (4 tests, 2 of them search) and OperatorServiceTest (list and search cases: 12 tests). Covered: the one list endpoint, its three query parameters (page, q, countryCode) with defaults, trimming and blank handling, its responses (200, 400 out-of-range or non-numeric page or missing header, 404, 500), the page size (server-configured, default 25, request parameters ignored), 1-based page numbering and the totals, every field of the page response, the search rules (fields matched, case-insensitive, partial, literal not regex, multi-word as one phrase), the OR combination of q and countryCode, the countryCode exact match, newest-first sort with an id tie-break, the ACTIVE-only and organisation-only listing, and the cv-025 and cv-048 rulings. The single-address operations, the address fields and validation, and the identity filter belong to other parts and are claimed only where the list operation depends on them.
Part 4, Organisation scoping and caller identity: Part 4, organisation scoping and caller identity. Read in full: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/filter/IdentityHeaderFilter.java (180 lines: the one identity header, its presence and format checks, the /organisation/ path test that decides which requests are checked, the path-orgId versus header comparison, the self-written problem+json rejections, the logging context and the trust-boundary Javadoc); src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/addressbook/address/OperatorController.java (368 lines, read for the class-level scoping, the authoriseOrg guard and the identity-header parameter on all five operations; per-endpoint behaviour left to parts 2 and 3); README.md section 'Security and trust boundary' (lines 83-109, plus the scoping sentence at the head of 'API overview', lines 113-115); src/test/java/.../filter/IdentityHeaderFilterTest.java (12 unit tests); src/test/java/.../integration/AddressScopingIT.java (7 integration tests). Covered: the single identity header the service reads (Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id) and every rejection when it is missing, blank or malformed; the exemption of every path outside /organisation/; the 404 for a path orgId that disagrees with the header, at both the filter and the controller guard; that the stored and queried organisation always comes from the header; cross-organisation isolation for list, read, create, update and delete; the no-existence-disclosure rule for 404s; the trust boundary in general terms; and what each of the 19 tests proves. Gaps recorded where the slice is silent: no user-level identity, no proof that a filter-level mismatch 404 matches an unknown-id 404 byte for byte, and no in-service enforcement of the upstream boundary.

claims.statement: An address-book entry is untyped and owned by an organisation: it has no type or role, and no operator-type categorisation.

claims.statement: An address is one flat set of fields (the Standard Address Block), with no nested address object.
claims.quote: The field set is flat — the Standard Address Block is one flat form, so there is no nested {@code Address} value object.

claims.quote: {@code countryCode} is stored as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (cv-011), exactly as supplied — the service does not convert it to or from a display name.

claims.statement: createdAt is set automatically when an address is first saved, and modifiedAt is updated automatically on every write, including an update and a soft delete.
